text: That is a very important clue, as hip pain often refers to the knee in children. Do you have a history of fever, rash, or recent illness, and does the pain get worse at night?

text: Let me examine your hips to check for any limitation in movement or tenderness. I will gently move your legs to see how your hip joint responds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That limited internal rotation and referred knee pain strongly suggest a hip issue. Are you experiencing any pain with walking or running, and has your gait changed significantly over the past two weeks?

text: Based on your symptoms of referred knee pain, limited internal rotation of the hip, and a painless limp, I am highly suspicious of slipped capital femoral epiphysis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE)
